actions.action: Tip the plant out of the pot and inspect roots for rot
If roots are mostly rotted, trim them back to firm tissue
Push a finger 1-2 inches into the soil to check moisture before watering
If soil is dry and pulling away from the pot, give a deep thorough soak
Mix perlite, pumice or bark into the current soil at about 1:3 to improve drainage
Water when the top inch of soil is dry
Empty the built-in tray after every watering
Move the plant to bright, indirect light away from direct sun
Remove leaves that are fully yellow or brown
Check leaf undersides for spider mites or thrips

reason: The answer leads with sun scorch and treats wet, dense soil as a secondary root-stress factor, so the diagnosis is partial; amending the soil and emptying the tray approach the repot fix, but it explicitly says no full repot is needed, so the advice is partial; nothing in it is likely to worsen the plant.
